title: Archway over La Silla
caption: The Milky Way over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The intricate glow of the Milky Way forms an arch over ESO's La Silla Observatory in northern Chile. Below it stand two linked domes, ESO's 3.6-meter telescope on the left and the decommissioned Coudé Auxiliary Telescope on the right, joined by a bridge.
Although the Coudé Auxiliary Telescope has been decommissioned, both domes still reach up toward the sky, as if straining for a closer look at the galaxy above.

Overhead, the Milky Way is our own galaxy seen from within. We live inside a flattened disc of stars, gas and dust, so when we look along it, the combined light of distant stars forms a band across the sky. Darker lanes and patches are clouds of dust in front of the starlight. Under a dark sky like La Silla's, those details become rich and complex, which is what gives the arch its intricate look.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure collects much more light than the eye can, so the Milky Way appears brighter and more detailed here than it would to a visitor.
